critical_code_review_comments: server.py /api/admin/scrape: live scrape runs synchronously in a thread (asyncio.to_thread). With a 8s/30s timeout an admin double-clicking the button could queue multiple HTTP fetches. Consider a global asyncio.Lock or a simple in-flight flag in _LIVE_POOL_CACHE.
server.py startup _seed swallows ALL exceptions silently with bare 'except Exception: pass' — startup scrape failures are invisible. At minimum log the failure (logger.warning).

lottery_data.scrape_live_4d (sync requests call) is invoked from async via to_thread, which is fine, but the request timeout (5-8s) blocks app startup. Better: schedule scraping as a fire-and-forget asyncio.Task after app is ready, not inside @app.on_event('startup') awaited.
AdminPage Inject form: empty 'raw_text' will hit the 400 from backend; UI does not disable the button when input is empty. Minor UX hole.
ADMIN_EMAILS parsing in server.py uses comma split + lowercase strip — good. But there is no log on startup of how many admins were configured (helpful for debugging).
serialize_user computes is_admin on the fly from ADMIN_EMAILS env — correct and avoids stale DB flags; well done.

Iteration-2 carry-over: CORS allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=True still present in server.py (line 133-139). Browsers reject credentialed CORS with wildcard origin per spec; pin to actual frontend URL via CORS_ORIGINS env (already defined but unused).
/api/admin/draws GET limits to 200 docs and bundled_count loops every call — fine at current scale, but consider caching ld.HISTORICAL_RESULTS counts module-level.
